procedure: Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy for Chronic Wounds/TBI/Lyme
estimated_cost_range_usd: $150-350 per session, typical 20-40 sessions = $3,000-14,000. Insurance covers FDA indications. Off-label: cash-pay model.
access_pathway_details: HBOT widely available at hospitals, wound centers, and specialized HBOT clinics across all 50 states. FDA-approved indications covered by insurance. Off-label indications available through specialized clinics (less insurance coverage). Prescriber must be MD/DO trained in HBOT.
eligibility_requirements: Medical evaluation confirming FDA or off-label indication. Baseline oxygen testing. Pulmonary evaluation for some indications. Psychological screening may be recommended for chronic conditions.
provider_requirements: HBOT-trained physician prescriber (varies by state: some require ABPM board certification in HBOT). Technician NBDHBO-certified (board certified). HYPOC accreditation for chamber standards.
residency_travel_notes: Available nationwide. Non-residents can travel for treatment (typically 20-40 sessions over 4-8 weeks, requires extended stay for optimal therapy).
risk_notes: Physical: claustrophobia (mitigated with open chambers), middle ear/sinus barotrauma (common, manageable), pulmonary oxygen toxicity (rare at medical protocols). Seizures from oxygen toxicity (very rare). Eye myopia (transient). Well-established safety profile when protocols followed.
oversight_notes: FDA regulation of chamber equipment (device classification). State medical board oversight of prescribers. HYPOC voluntary chamber accreditation. Insurance companies require credentialing for coverage. Higher oversight for FDA-approved vs. off-label indications.
cost_notes: FDA-approved indications: insurance coverage typical (Medicare, commercial). Off-label: cash-pay. Some clinics offer treatment packages at discounts. $150–350/session mid $250; 20–40 session courses $3–14k. FDA indications often insured.
arbitrage_summary: FDA-approved HBOT widely accessible at high-oversight centers. Off-label use (Lyme, TBI) available but uninsured. Cost-effectiveness depends on indication and insurance coverage.
